items.title: John Beal interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2024
items.q: There was a book called — now I can’t remember, damn — The Agony of Modern Music by Henry Pleasants. And he said the real modern music is jazz...

ctx.x: Do you think modern classical music is — I’m not sure where “modern” starts but — more difficult to play than the classics, the Romantic period and Baroque music? That’s a wide question but I once had an experience playing a Honegger piece and there was a saxophone part and man I could not keep track of where it was. It was so harmonically dense and of course they had 60 bars of rest before I came in and talk about sweating. Please give me a cue.

Yeah. Well you know you’re getting into a controversial area you know. There was a book called — now I can’t remember, damn — The Agony of Modern Music by Henry Pleasants. And he said the real modern music is jazz, because like from Stravinsky on you know it got so complicated with different time signatures and it’s like a made-up idiom sort of because the complexity of playing contemporary music, it’s like you don’t know what style — I mean you have to learn the style of each individual composer but it’s like —…

It seems like the music composition in the classical world keeps trying to do something new and I think it might have to do with getting a grant — getting grants to write new work and how far can you go and still do something new? And what we get is what maybe you’re struggling to find in your description.
